correctness.rationale: Direct finite antipodal-geodesic averaging bounds the fractional objective by t*2^(d-1). Equality on each antipodal path implies both independent square-route equalities, hence opposite square edges match. Connectedness of the square-flip graph on each direction class forces one weight per coordinate; the optimal face is exactly Delta(d,t). Integer coordinates select t classes, counted by binomial(d,t). All definitions, ranges including d=t=2, normalization, and converse are checked. Independent-implementation finite tests exhaust Q2 and Q3 and an exact MILP optimal-enumeration certifies Q4 for t=2,3; finite tests are not used to justify the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The most relevant 2021 and 2022 full-text theorems establish only optimum cardinalities and examples of maximizing coordinate classes, with no equality-case necessity or fractional-face theorem. The full 2023 and 2024 studies involve different graph families. An older finite Q4 classification is acknowledged as covered in one instance, but it cannot subsume the uniform structural theorem. Search comparisons found no dominating statement; publication priority is provisional.
residual_risks: Publication-index incompleteness may conceal equivalent cube equality-case results under polyhedral, path-packing, or linear programming terminology.
The 2025 subscription-gated article was inspected at abstract level only; no negative full-text claim is made.
A previously obtained finite Q4 optimizer census is covered and expressly not claimed as new.

value.rationale: The prior all-capacity numeric formula permits many a priori different optimal edge patterns. The new nontrivial square saturation lemma proves global rigidity across every dimension and capacity, simultaneously identifies the complete fractional optimum face with an (often high-dimensional) hypersimplex, and counts all integral maximizers. These solve natural equality and optimizer classification questions rather than reiterating the known numerical extremum.
